title: Have Citizens Insurance? You'll Need Flood Coverage in 2027
dek: Starting January 1, every Citizens homeowners policy with wind coverage needs a separate flood policy to renew, in any flood zone. The federal flood program is set to expire December 11.
body:
Yes. If you have a homeowners policy with Citizens Property Insurance that covers wind, you will need a separate flood insurance policy for Citizens to renew it on or after January 1, 2027, no matter what your home is worth or what FEMA flood zone it sits in. Condo unit owner policies, renters policies and policies that leave out wind are exempt.

The rule has been phasing in since 2024, and January is the last step, when it reaches every Citizens homeowner regardless of value. It lands at an awkward moment. The National Flood Insurance Program, where most Floridians buy flood coverage, is only authorized through December 11, and new federal flood policies usually take 30 days to start.

Who has to carry flood insurance

Citizens applies the rule to most new and renewing personal residential policies that include wind coverage. Homes in FEMA's high risk zones, the A and V zones, already had to carry flood insurance. For everyone else, the requirement has stepped down by the home's dwelling coverage, known as Coverage A, according to Citizens:

Policies written or renewed on or afterFlood insurance required if Coverage A is
January 1, 2024$600,000 or more
January 1, 2025$500,000 or more
January 1, 2026$400,000 or more
January 1, 2027Any amount

Three kinds of policies are exempt: condo unit owner policies, renters policies and policies that exclude wind and hail. If you carry a wind only policy with Citizens, the flood requirement still applies, and Citizens asks to see a flood endorsement on the underlying policy. Hillsborough County warned residents on November 13 that owners without flood coverage risk being dropped when their policy comes up for renewal. Florida law is blunt about it: a home that doesn't meet the requirement is not eligible for Citizens coverage.

How much flood coverage you need

Your flood limit has to match or exceed your Citizens dwelling coverage. If that is more than the federal program will write, Citizens accepts the most you are eligible for, which is $250,000 for a home in the regular NFIP program. Flood insurance from a private company authorized to write it in Florida also counts. Citizens does not sell flood insurance itself.

To prove it, Citizens wants your flood declarations page, or if the policy hasn't been issued yet, the application and proof that you paid. It also asks for a signed form called the Policyholder Affirmation Regarding Flood Insurance.

What flood insurance costs in Florida

Less than many people expect, especially outside the high risk zones. NerdWallet's analysis of federal flood data, updated in May 2026, put the average NFIP policy in Florida at about $938 a year, roughly $78 a month, and about $637 a year in the lower risk zone X. That is well under the typical homeowners bill, which averaged about $3,750 a year statewide in the state's July 2026 numbers, as we laid out in our county by county insurance guide.

Plenty of people go without. An AM Best analyst told Insurance Journal this week that fewer than 20% of Florida property owners carry flood insurance. Citizens has also shrunk from about 1.4 million policies in 2023 to just above 200,000, and many owners who moved to a private insurer likely dropped the flood policy Citizens had required. Our guide to flood insurance outside a flood zone covers why that is a gamble even in zone X.

The December 11 problem

The federal flood program runs on short extensions from Congress, and the current one expires December 11, 2026. As of this week no new extension had passed. If the program lapses, the National Association of Realtors says it cannot issue new or renewal policies. Existing policies stay in force until they expire, claims keep getting paid while money lasts, and private flood insurance is not affected.

New NFIP policies normally take 30 days to start. The main exception is a policy bought when you take out, increase, extend or renew a mortgage, which can start right away. During the last lapse, in 2025, Citizens let policyholders hold off on sending flood paperwork, then required it by December 1, 2025 to avoid cancellation. There is no word yet on whether it would do the same again.

So if your Citizens policy renews in December or early next year, the simplest move is to buy flood coverage now, while the federal program can still write it, or get a quote from a private flood insurer.

Why this matters more after November

The storms of November 17 to 21 dumped well over a foot of rain on parts of east Florida. The St. Johns River near Cocoa crested at 18.68 feet on November 20, breaking a record that had stood since 1953, and AccuWeather reported that some flooding there could last into January. Earlier in the week, rain had already flooded homes outside FEMA's high risk zones in places like Palm Bay and Melbourne.

If you are shopping for a home, check the address against our flood rankings and ask the seller for the current flood policy and its premium. If the house is insured with Citizens today, flood coverage is now part of the price of keeping it there.
faq: Does Citizens require flood insurance in 2027?

Yes. Starting with policies written or renewed on or after January 1, 2027, Citizens requires flood insurance on personal residential policies that include wind coverage, regardless of the home's value or FEMA flood zone.
Do Citizens condo owners need flood insurance?
No. Condo unit owner policies are exempt from the Citizens flood requirement, along with renters policies and policies that exclude wind.
How much flood coverage does Citizens require?

Your flood limit has to equal or exceed your Citizens dwelling coverage. If that is more than the NFIP will write, Citizens accepts the program maximum you qualify for, which is $250,000 for a home in the regular program.
Can I use private flood insurance for Citizens?
Yes. Citizens accepts flood coverage from the NFIP or from a private insurer authorized to write flood insurance in Florida.
What happens if the NFIP lapses on December 11, 2026?
The NFIP could not issue new or renewal policies until Congress acts. Existing policies stay in force until they expire, claims are still paid, and private flood insurance is not affected.
